minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard FY22 budgets from Council on Aging, Library and Land Use; minutes approved pending amendment.
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY22 departmental budget presentations from the Council on Aging, the Library and the land use director, with questions on off-budget funding, line increases and salary reserve treatment of union contracts. Karen briefed on materials for next week's debt and OPEB session. Minutes from three earlier meetings were approved pending amendments, and department reports were given before adjournment.

passed by roll call, all members voting aye

budget_items.what_was_said: Director said the department is level funded with no increase requested; the year-over-year increase is all salary.
Governor's budget would cut the per-elder formula grant; depends on census timing for the count used.
Mileage goes mostly to Meals on Wheels volunteer drivers; some may be turned back this year.
Formula grant is outside the town budget and pays two employees, trainings, supplies and a database renewal.
A member noted personnel lines rise despite level program dollars; longevity pay and a possible cap through the personnel committee and Town Meeting were discussed.
Library municipal budget, outside funding and the state-required appropriation threshold were reviewed; request is about one percent above FY21, close to the town manager's preliminary figure.
Carpet replacement is funded through capital and an RFP is being prepared.
State requires a share of appropriation go to materials; director requests increases to the book service and materials lines, with more for e-materials.
Population growth moves the library into full membership with a three-year phase-in; the network budget line is requested to rise.
Five thousand in FY21 was a one-time strategic plan consultant; a lower amount is requested for FY22.
Hannaford gave funds for a children's room tween space.
Union step eight position is nearly flat; contract increases would be funded from the salary reserve.
Increase to buy new code books as the state adopts the 2021 code.
Permit fees go to the general fund and are intended to match the cost of the service.
A GIS license was purchased so staff can view contractors' stormwater data.

Next meeting set for the 25th at 6 p.m.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY22 budget presentations from the Council on Aging, the Library and the land use director; no budget votes were taken.
The Council on Aging director said the department is level funded, with the year-over-year increase all in salary.
The Council on Aging director agreed to send the committee her sheet of revenue sources outside the town budget the next day.
The Library's request is about one percent above FY21; the director asked for more in materials and the CW MARS network line as state requirements and membership change.
Minutes from three earlier meetings were approved pending amendments, and the next meeting was set for the 25th at 6 p.m.

why_it_matters: Council on Aging and Library costs rise even with level programs, through salary steps and state-driven requirements, and the committee's questions on salary reserve and off-budget funding bear on how much of the FY22 tax levy those departments draw.
The Council on Aging's state formula grant sits outside the town budget and pays staff, so a cut in the Governor's budget could shift those costs onto the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The Council on Aging's sheet of outside revenue sources, due to the committee the day after the meeting.
The debt schedules and OPEB presentation to be emailed to members, ahead of the committee's meeting on the 25th at 6 p.m.
